record: Arrival by wagon, and the camp: step 2 of docs/SETTLING_IN.md
verdictMeaning: A new class begins with every family - its people, ox, horse and wagon - at the fork where its own track leaves the road, on the road in at the wagon's pace (0.65 miles a tick). Nobody and nothing is placed at a homestead. The family arrives together, stands about its yard as a family always has, goes back to what it was doing, and its record says so once. There is no house: the family camps by the wagon, where rest mends at two-thirds the rate and 3 in 100 of the food spoils a day, and its land line says both numbers. A family rolled in the lobby goes on the road beside its wagon. A class saved before arrivals is housed, camps nowhere, and plays as it did; no save version moved.
implementation: sim/settling.mjs: beginArrivals (called by createGonzalesWorld, only for a class with director.arrival) sets improvements.cabin to 'none', puts every member and piece of property on a journey with purpose 'arrive', silent, carrying settle {x, y, task}, and corrects the founding line in place. progressTravel ends a journey at settle's spot and task when it has one. advanceArrivals runs after travel each tick and records one 'arrival' event per family. routines.mjs reads housed(): rest at the family's own land mends at CAMP_REST_SHARE, and food is multiplied by 1 - CAMP_SPOILAGE_PER_DAY x days. The land projection gains shelter, arriving and camp; the tick gains arrivalClass.
timings: Tracks from fork to homestead measured 0.8 to 13.2 miles across seeds for 5, 15 and 30 families: 2 to 21 ticks, 40 minutes to 7 hours of the family's time, 19 seconds to 3.3 real minutes at the Study pace. The notice is at tick 84.
art: No stand-in. The camp is drawn from the library's road-camp kit - campfire (animated by fire-flicker), cooking-pot, bedroll, packed-belongings - and the wagon is drawn where it actually is, as property.

observed: Lobby, before rolling: '1835-09-28 · waiting to begin'; the family's wagon and people drawn at their fork on the road; camps (fire, bundles, bedroll) drawn at the student's own land and at two neighbours' homesteads, and no cabins.
Rolled a 5: all five people, the ox, the mare and the wagon on the road to home-2 at progress 0, people's task 'travel'.

Land line on the road: 'Their land: they are still on the road in with the wagon. There is no house yet, so they camp by the wagon: rest there mends 67 parts in 100 of what it would under a roof, and 3 parts in 100 of the food spoil each day.'
Walk-through on the road: all five steps readable, none disabled or waiting; step 2 says work cannot start on the road instead of waiting for a chore.

Started as Host. Minute 160: 'The family has reached its own land. There is no house yet, so they camp by the wagon.' Amos and Rhoda at work, the three children resting, all at home-2; the camp drawn beside the wagon and ox with fire-flicker playing; the selection panel offered Plant the field.

automated.testsChanged: Farming, hunting, powder, practice, store, money, fatigue, travel-mode, improvement and aggregate tests now build their class with tests/support/settled.mjs, which finishes every arrival on the spot and stands a cabin - the world they were written for. decisions and family-effects likewise; family-roll settles two fixtures; the peaceful-opening farm test waits for the real arrival. The fresh-snapshot size bounds in geography and family tests rose from 8192 and 7000 to 10240 bytes: a family on the road carries a journey and a refusal for every job, about 9.1 KB, until it arrives.

boundary: Until step 4 no family can build a house, so a class started on this build camps all game. Neighbours' homesteads are drawn as camps because the class began with arrivals (arrivalClass), not because anybody saw them - a ceiling that step 4 must replace. Only food spoils; only the family's own land is a camp; there is no night.
